author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Runners left Boston carrying two American flags on a 228-mile relay to Ground Zero, marking 25 years since the September 11 attacks and honoring the people killed.

The flags represent the two hijacked planes that departed Logan International Airport. Relay for America organized the route as a symbolic effort to retrace and reclaim the path from Boston to New York through remembrance and public service.

Each relay segment is 9.11 miles. Boston police escorted the first leg, and organizers said police or fire escorts were confirmed for 20 portions of the journey. First responders are also joining runners along the route.

The nonstop relay is designed to connect communities between the two cities while keeping the victims’ names and the role of emergency personnel in public view. Its arrival at Ground Zero will coincide with anniversary observances in New York. Organizers framed the run not as a race but as a moving memorial carried from the airport where the flights began to the site where many of the victims died.
dek: Relay for America runners are carrying two flags along the route associated with the planes that departed Logan Airport on September 11, 2001.
headline: Flag relay begins 228-mile journey from Boston to Ground Zero
location: Boston, MA to New York, NY
